record.paper_title: Modeling social resilience: Questions, answers, open problems
record.original_question: For a signed social-organization network decomposed into triads, how can structural robustness be measured so that triads are not treated as independent, relation weights are incorporated, and the importance or impact of the agents in each triad affects the collective robustness estimate?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G = (V, E, s, w, \alpha) be a finite signed weighted social network, where:
- V is a set of agents,
- E \subseteq \binom{V}{2} is the set of relations,
- s : E \to \{+1, -1\} assigns a sign (positive/negative tie) to every relation,
- w : E \to \mathbb{R}_{>0} assigns a positive weight (interaction strength) to every relation,
- \alpha : V \to \mathbb{R}_{>0} assigns an importance/impact score to every agent.

Let T(G) denote the multiset of triads (3-cliques) of G. For a triad t = \{i,j,k\} \in T(G), call t balanced if the product s(ij)\,s(jk)\,s(ik) = +1, and unbalanced otherwise. Note that triads may share vertices or edges, so they are not independent.

Design a real-valued functional
R : (G) \longmapsto R(G) \in \mathbb{R},
called the structural robustness of G, satisfying simultaneously the following requirements:

(R1) Non-independence of triads. R(G) must not be expressible as a sum (or other separable aggregation) over T(G) that treats triads as statistically or structurally independent; it must explicitly account for the overlap structure of shared edges and shared agents among triads.

(R2) Weight incorporation. R(G) must depend on the relation weights w(e), not only on the signs s(e), in such a way that strengthening (resp. weakening) a balanced relation increases (resp. decreases) R(G), and strengthening an unbalanced relation decreases R(G).

(R3) Agent-impact sensitivity. R(G) must depend on the agent importance values \alpha(i): in any triad t = \{i,j,k\}, the contribution of t to R(G) must be modulated by \alpha(i), \alpha(j), \alpha(k), so that triads containing more impactful agents contribute more strongly to the collective robustness estimate.

Provide an explicit construction of such an R, together with axioms characterizing it (e.g. monotonicity under sign flips, continuity in w and \alpha, behavior under disjoint union and under edge deletion), and prove that the proposed functional satisfies (R1)–(R3).
artifact.category_tag: Weighted structural balance in signed networks
artifact.status_search_result: The literature contains several partial approaches: weighted node-to-node influence models for structural balance, multilevel evaluation of signed digraphs based on balance theory, dynamic weight-evolution frameworks, and attention-based triad weighting for embeddings. However, none of these provides a single agreed-upon robustness functional that simultaneously (i) handles triad overlap rather than independence, (ii) incorporates relation weights, and (iii) integrates agent importance. The problem is posed as an open discussion item and remains open in this combined form.

status_evidence.title: An improved network structural balance approach based on weighted node-to-node influence
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes weighted node-to-node influence models for the structural balance problem in weighted signed social networks.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses weights but not the combined criteria of overlap and agent-impact-sensitive robustness.

status_evidence.title: Multilevel structural evaluation of signed directed social networks based on balance theory
status_evidence.snippet: Multilevel evaluation of balance in signed digraphs, treating triads at multiple aggregation levels.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on overlap, but does not give a unified weighted, agent-importance-sensitive robustness measure.

status_evidence.title: Attending Over Triads for Learning Signed Network Embedding
status_evidence.snippet: Uses attention to weight triads by importance for embedding tasks.
status_evidence.claim: Provides triad-importance weighting heuristics but not a principled robustness functional.

status_evidence.title: Structural Balance under Weight Evolution of Dynamic Signed Network
status_evidence.snippet: Studies how edge weights evolve while balance is maintained.
status_evidence.claim: Treats weight dynamics but not collective robustness with agent-impact terms.
